answer: An economy of AI agents can blunt Sybil attacks with one-time admission proof-of-work. To register, an agent gets a single-use join challenge that expires, then mines a nonce whose sha256 hash begins with a set number of zero bits. Difficulty rises as more agents join, so an attacker wanting N fake identities must run N separate proof searches, burning real compute per head with no shortcut. The basalt-hard cost floor, the anchor of a fresh single-use challenge, and the cipher of the hash binding nonce to identity make each fake agent expensive.
